question: CONTRIB's audit row says the first commit after the audited sha that is neither in the records set nor a fix commit voids the audit. So a branch that merged dev forward has to re-run its audit?
premise_flaw: no, and the rule as written did void every branch that had dispatched anything, because dispatch.sh merges the trunk forward before every launch (agentscient-11, 2026-09-16, measured on #242). The gate walks <audited>..<head> first-parent, skips merge commits and drops anything reachable from origin/<trunk>, so only the branch's own commits are judged. The branch's own commit after that merge still voids it and is still named in the refusal; a trunk ref the clone cannot resolve is absent, not an empty exclusion, and every commit in the range is judged instead.
expect: only the branch's own commits are judged
